title: Data classes
context: What does the `data` modifier generate for a class, and what must its primary constructor contain?

refs.title: Atomic Kotlin (book) by Bruce Eckel & Svetlana Isakova

answer: A data class generates equals, hashCode, toString, copy and componentN functions based on the properties in the primary constructor. Equality is structural, so two instances with the same property values are equal. copy lets you make a changed copy without mutating the original. The primary constructor needs at least one val or var parameter. Only properties declared in the primary constructor take part in equals and hashCode. Data classes are final and can't be abstract, open, sealed or inner.

points.title: Generated functions
points.why: equals, hashCode, toString, copy and componentN are generated from the constructor properties.

points.title: Constructor rules
points.why: The primary constructor must have at least one val or var parameter.

points.title: Properties outside the constructor
points.why: Body properties are not part of equality or copy, which surprises people.
